summary: Honduras's own per-nationality visa list is no longer online, so this page gives the entry rule only for passports an official source still states. The National Institute of Migration says a tourist may stay up to 90 days, extendable by 30 days, and distinguishes a consular visa from a "consulted" visa that it must validate first. It says citizens of Guatemala, El Salvador and Nicaragua can use a national identity card or a passport under the CA-4 agreement. The Institute runs an online immigration pre-check (prechequeo).

tips.text: You can do the online immigration pre-check at prechequeo.inm.gob.hn and download it to present to the immigration inspector. No official source we could read says whether it is mandatory.

Canada's travel advice says Canadian tourists can travel between Honduras, Guatemala, El Salvador and Nicaragua (the CA-4) for up to 90 days, that an extension of up to 30 days must be requested from the National Migration Institute before the first stay expires, and that Honduras allows a maximum of 120 days.

If you dive in the Bay Islands, the UK FCDO says there is a hyperbaric (recompression) chamber on Roatán and recompression facilities on Utila, but that emergency medical facilities on the islands are extremely limited.

The UK FCDO advises avoiding walking around Tegucigalpa, San Pedro Sula and other main towns and cities in mainland Honduras, using radio-dispatched or hotel taxis for shorter distances, considering alternatives to public buses, and not displaying phones, jewellery or other valuables.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Honduras?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport, and Honduras's own per-nationality visa list is no longer online. Foreign governments' travel advice says Canadian, Dutch and Italian citizens need no visa for stays of up to 90 days, and the UK Foreign Office says British citizens must have one. The National Institute of Migration says tourists may stay up to 90 days, extendable by 30, and distinguishes a consular visa from a "consulted" visa that it must validate first.

faq.question: What is the Honduras prechequeo form?
faq.answer: An online immigration pre-check (prechequeo migratorio) run by Honduras's National Migration Institute at prechequeo.inm.gob.hn. You receive a one-time token by email to do the pre-check in its application, and can download your pre-check to present to the immigration inspector. No official source we could read says whether it is mandatory.

faq.question: How does the CA-4 90-day rule work in Honduras?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says that under the CA-4 agreement Canadian tourists can travel between Honduras, Guatemala, El Salvador and Nicaragua for up to 90 days, with the length of stay set by the immigration officer at the first entry point. An extension of up to 30 days must be requested and paid for at the National Migration Institute before the first stay expires, and Honduras allows a maximum of 120 days; after that you must change your status, leave the CA-4 region or travel to El Salvador.

faq.question: Is Honduras safe for tourists?
faq.answer: The UK FCDO says Honduras has one of the highest violent crime rates in Latin America; most serious crime does not affect tourists, but incidents can happen anywhere, even in tourist areas. Canada says the Bay Islands are generally safe, with lower violent crime, and advises avoiding non-essential travel to some areas, including within 20 km of the borders with Guatemala and El Salvador (with listed exceptions such as Copán Ruinas and the El Florido crossing) and the eastern neighbourhoods of San Pedro Sula. Both advise avoiding road travel at night.

faq.question: Can I pay in US dollars on Roatán?
faq.answer: The UK FCDO says US dollars are widely accepted for exchange and payment in Honduras, and that British pounds are difficult to exchange. It advises checking with your hotel which ATMs to use, especially in Roatán.

faq.ca4.text: Under the terms of the Central America-4 Border Control Agreement (CA-4), Canadian tourists may travel freely within any of the following CA-4 countries: El Salvador Guatemala Honduras Nicaragua You can travel between these countries for up to 90 days without having to undergo entry and exit formalities at border immigration checkpoints.
The immigration officer at your first entry point into the CA-4 region will determine the exact length of your authorized stay.
You may request an extension of up to 30 days. However, you must request this extension and pay the required fee at the National Migration Institute before your first authorized stay expires.
You are authorized to stay in Honduras for a maximum of 120 days.
Once your total authorized stay expires, you must either: change your migratory status leave the CA-4 region travel to El Salvador
